content:
alex: heads up — noticed a regression on canary yesterday, 95th latency for short prompts jumped ~30% after the kernel-selector change. ran an nsys trace and the timeline shows a tight loop in the selector with lots of tiny kernel dispatches + KV cache misses. attaching initial qdrep: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1955554321_canary_nsight.qdrep (public to team)
maria: ugh. do you have the timeline snapshot? can you paste the hot region name you saw in nsight?
alex: screenshot attached in the trace link. hot region is the kernel chooser loop — shows repeated calls into `choose_kernel_for_request` and then `dispatch_kernel`, lots of small kernels of ~200-800us each. KV cache shows spikes of misses around the same request intervals.
sam: sounds like two separate problems: kernel selector doing too much work per-request, and KV cache contention/async prefetch not hitting. both could be amplification from batching heuristics change.
alex: yep. i'm thinking we add NVTX ranges in three places so we can stitch perfetto timelines + nsys: 1) per-request span: `req.{shortid}` (begin/end) 2) `runtime.kv.lookup` / `runtime.kv.prefetch` 3) `runtime.kernel.select` and `runtime.kernel.dispatch`
maria: +1 on the ranges. couple of constraints: NVTX overhead if we push/pop per-token is real. prefer per-request or per-batch ranges, not per-token. also we should standardize names to make traces queryable.
jordan: proposal for naming convention: `rt:<area>:<op>:<tag>` e.g. `rt:kv:lookup:hit` or `rt:kern:select:fastpath`. keep short but structured. use `req:<id>` outside of these ranges to group.
sam: agree. also add an attribute inside NVTX (nvtxRangePushEx) with a short hex request id so we can grep. Perfetto can show args as well.
perf-bot: reminder — NVTX metadata size affects capture. try to keep arg strings <= 64 chars.
maria: for the KV cache, instrument three micro-ranges: `rt:kv:prefetch`, `rt:kv:backend_fetch`, `rt:kv:lookup:hit/miss`. For backend fetches we can add an internal `fetch_size` counter as a perf counter instead of pushing more ranges.
alex: implementation note: in C++ runtime we can add helper macros: ```
#define NVTX_PUSH(name) nvtxRangePushA(name)
#define NVTX_POP() nvtxRangePop()
```
but for request spans use `nvtxRangeId_t id = nvtxRangeStartEx(&params); nvtxRangeEnd(id);` so we can attach numeric id.
jordan: important to avoid calling NVTX inside the hot selector loop every iteration. I think we should 1) push a `rt:kern:select` range that covers the whole selection work for the request (not per branch) and 2) add a lightweight perf counter for branch counts inside the selector to catch the frequency of slow paths.
sam: +1. also check kernel queueing: the nsys shows a lot of tiny CUDA kernels, maybe our batching boundaries are fragmenting batches. We should instrument `rt:batch:merge` and `rt:batch:seal` around the batch builder.
maria: testing plan: add ranges in a feature branch `perf/nvtx-kv-kernel-2026`, run `nsys profile -o nvtx_kv_run --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=none --cpuctx` on a canary workload, then upload qdrep + capture perfetto proto using `nsys export --report=timeline` and `perfetto` with chrome tracing view.
alex: example commands i ran: ```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda --capture-range=none --force-overwrite --cuda-attach=all ./bin/runtime_canary --workload short_prompts
perfetto --config trace_config.pbtxt --out=/tmp/trace.pb
``` 
I also enabled `KVCACHE_PREFETCH=1` in that run to see prefetch timing.
perf-bot: note: upload size limit is 10GB for traces; consider sampling if you exceed rdf.
jordan: metrics to collect: 95th/99th latency per-route, kernel dispatch count per-request, kv lookup miss rate, avg batch size. We'll surface these in Console as temporary charts.
sam: i can add the NVTX wrappers and the batch ranges. alex, can you add the perf counters for selector branches? maria can you own the kvcache microranges and the test runs?
alex: yep. i'll open the PR shortly — will include a minimal flag to enable NVTX ranges at runtime `--enable-trace-ranges` so we don't pay overhead in prod by default.
maria: when you open the PR, include a small perf doc snippet in the PR description explaining why we chose per-request ranges vs per-token and the expected cost profile.
alex: will do. action items: alex (selector counters + PR), sam (nvtx wrappers + batch ranges), maria (kvcache microranges + test runs). i'll attach the first qdrep link and add follow-up traces. thanks all :thumbsup:
